units.zh: 廢帝皇后劉氏
units.en: Empress Liu, wife of the deposed Later Tang emperor.
units.literal: Empress Liu of the Deposed Emperor

units.zh: 廢帝皇后劉氏，父茂威，應州渾元人也。
units.en: Empress Liu, wife of the deposed emperor, was the daughter of Maowei of Hunyuan in Ying Prefecture.
units.literal: Empress Liu of the Deposed Emperor—her father was Maowei, a man of Hunyuan in Yingzhou.

units.zh: 后為人彊悍，廢帝素憚之。
units.en: She was fierce and domineering by nature, and the deposed emperor had always been afraid of her.
units.literal: The empress was by nature fierce and overbearing, and the Deposed Emperor had long feared her.

units.zh: 初封沛國夫人，廢帝即位，立為皇后。
units.en: She was first created Lady of Pei; when the deposed emperor acceded, she was enthroned as empress.
units.literal: At first she was enfeoffed as Lady of Pei; when the Deposed Emperor took the throne, she was made empress.

units.zh: 其弟延皓，少事廢帝為牙將，廢帝即位，拜宮苑使、宣徽南院使。
units.en: Her brother Yanhao had served the deposed emperor as a guards officer in his youth; on his accession Yanhao was made commissioner of the palace parks and of the southern court of the Bureau of Palace Attendants.
units.literal: Her younger brother Yanhao had served the Deposed Emperor in youth as a guards officer; when the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Yanhao was appointed Commissioner of the Palace Parks and Commissioner of the Southern Court of the Bureau of Palace Attendants.

units.zh: 清泰二年，為樞密使、天雄軍節度使。
units.en: In Qingtai 2 he was appointed commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and military governor of the Tianxiong Army.
units.literal: In Qingtai 2 he became Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and military governor of the Tianxiong Army.

units.zh: 延皓為人素謹厚，及貴而改節，以后故用事，受賕，掠人園宅，在鄴下不恤軍士，軍士皆怨。
units.en: Yanhao had been modest and honest, but once he rose in rank he changed his conduct; relying on his sister’s position he took power, accepted bribes, seized gardens and residences, and at Ye neglected the troops, who came to hate him.
units.literal: Yanhao had been plain and honest in character, but once elevated he changed his ways; because of his sister he wielded power, accepted bribes, seized others’ gardens and houses, and at Ye showed no care for the soldiers, so the troops all resented him.

units.zh: 捧聖都虞候張令昭以其屯駐兵逐延皓，延皓走相州。
units.en: Zhang Lingzhao, chief inspector of the Pengsheng command, expelled Yanhao with the troops stationed under him, and Yanhao fled to Xiangzhou.
units.literal: Zhang Lingzhao, chief inspector of the Pengsheng command, drove Yanhao out with the garrison troops under his command, and Yanhao fled to Xiangzhou.

units.zh: 是時，石敬瑭已反，方用兵，而令昭之亂作。
units.en: Shi Jingtang had already rebelled and fighting was under way when Lingzhao’s revolt erupted.
units.literal: At that time Shi Jingtang had already rebelled and war was underway when Lingzhao’s mutiny broke out.

units.zh: 令昭乃閉城，遣其副使邊仁嗣請己為節度使。
units.en: Lingzhao closed the city and sent his deputy Bian Rensi to ask that he be appointed military governor.
units.literal: Lingzhao then shut the city gates and sent his deputy Bian Rensi to request that he himself be made military governor.

units.zh: 廢帝以令昭為右千牛衞將軍，權知天雄軍府事。
units.en: The deposed emperor appointed Lingzhao general of the Right Thousand-Bull Guards and acting administrator of the Tianxiong headquarters.
units.literal: The Deposed Emperor made Lingzhao General of the Right Thousand-Bull Guards and acting administrator of the Tianxiong headquarters.

units.zh: 已而遣范延光討之，令昭敗走邢州，追至沙河，斬之，屯駐諸軍亂者三千餘人皆死。
units.en: He then sent Fan Yanguang against him; Lingzhao was defeated, fled to Xingzhou, was pursued to Shahe and executed, and more than three thousand mutinous garrison soldiers were killed.
units.literal: Soon afterward he sent Fan Yanguang to attack him; Lingzhao was defeated and fled to Xingzhou, was pursued to Shahe and beheaded, and more than three thousand mutinous garrison troops were put to death.

units.zh: 有司請以延皓行軍法，廢帝以后故，削其官爵而已。
units.en: Officials asked that Yanhao be punished under military law, but because of the empress the deposed emperor only removed his offices and titles.
units.literal: The authorities asked that Yanhao be dealt with under military law, but because of the empress the Deposed Emperor merely stripped him of office and rank.

units.zh: 廢帝二子
units.en: The deposed emperor’s two sons.
units.literal: The Two Sons of the Deposed Emperor

units.zh: 廢帝二子，曰重吉、重美，一女為尼，號幼澄，皆不知其所生。
units.en: His sons bore the names Chongji and Chongmei; a daughter took vows as a nun under the sobriquet Youcheng. History does not record who bore any of them.
units.literal: The Deposed Emperor’s two sons were named Chongji and Chongmei; one daughter became a Buddhist nun, styled Youcheng; none of them is known by whom they were born.

units.zh: 廢帝鎮鳳翔，重吉為控鶴指揮使，與尼俱留京師。
units.en: While the deposed emperor governed Fengxiang, Chongji served as commander of the Crane-Controlled Guard and stayed in the capital with the nun.
units.literal: When the Deposed Emperor held Fengxiang, Chongji was commander of the Crane-Controlled Guard and remained in the capital together with the nun.

units.zh: 控鶴，親兵也。
units.en: The Crane-Controlled were the sovereign’s personal guard.
units.literal: The Crane-Controlled were the emperor’s personal troops.

units.zh: 愍帝即位，不欲重吉掌親兵，乃出重吉為亳州團練使，居幼澄於禁中，又徙廢帝北京。
units.en: When the Min emperor acceded, unwilling to let Chongji command the personal guard, he posted Chongji to Bozhou as regimental commissioner, kept Youcheng in the inner palace, and transferred the deposed emperor to the northern capital.
units.literal: When the Min Emperor took the throne, he did not wish Chongji to command the personal guard, so he sent Chongji out as regimental commissioner of Bozhou, kept Youcheng within the palace, and also moved the Deposed Emperor to the northern capital.

units.zh: 廢帝自疑，乃反。
units.en: The deposed emperor grew suspicious and rose in revolt.
units.literal: The Deposed Emperor grew suspicious and rebelled.

units.zh: 愍帝遣人殺重吉于宋州，幼澄亦死。
units.en: The Min emperor sent agents to kill Chongji at Songzhou, and Youcheng died as well.
units.literal: The Min Emperor sent men to kill Chongji at Songzhou, and Youcheng also died.

units.zh: 重美，幼而明敏如成人。
units.en: Chongmei had been clever and quick-witted from childhood, like a grown man.
units.literal: Chongmei from childhood was bright and keen like an adult.

units.zh: 廢帝即位，自左衞上將軍領成德軍節度使、兼河南尹、判六軍諸衞事，改領天雄軍節度使、同中書門下平章事，封雍王。
units.en: When the deposed emperor acceded, Chongmei advanced from general of the Left Guard to military governor of the Chengde Army, concurrently grand guardian of Henan and overseer of the Six Armies and all guards; he was then transferred to military governor of the Tianxiong Army, made grand councilor, and enfeoffed as Prince of Yong.
units.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Chongmei rose from General of the Left Guard to military governor of the Chengde Army, concurrently Grand Guardian of Henan and overseer of the Six Armies and all guards; he was then transferred to military governor of the Tianxiong Army, made Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and enfeoffed as Prince of Yong.

units.zh: 石敬瑭反，廢帝欲北征，重美謂宜持重，固請毋行。
units.en: When Shi Jingtang rebelled, the deposed emperor wanted to march north; Chongmei urged caution and firmly pleaded that he not go.
units.literal: When Shi Jingtang rebelled, the Deposed Emperor wished to campaign north; Chongmei said he should act with restraint and firmly begged him not to go.

units.zh: 廢帝心憚敬瑭，初不欲往，聞重美言，以為然，而劉延皓與劉延朗等迫之不已，廢帝遂如河陽，留重美守京師。
units.en: The deposed emperor feared Jingtang and at first did not want to march; hearing Chongmei, he agreed, but Liu Yanhao, Liu Yanlang, and others kept pressing him, so he proceeded to Heyang and left Chongmei to hold the capital.
units.literal: The Deposed Emperor inwardly feared Jingtang and at first did not wish to go; hearing Chongmei’s words, he thought them right, but Liu Yanhao, Liu Yanlang, and others pressed him without cease, so the Deposed Emperor went on to Heyang and left Chongmei to guard the capital.

units.zh: 京師震恐，居民皆出城以藏竄，門者禁止之。
units.en: The capital was gripped by panic; residents fled the city to hide, and gatekeepers tried to stop them.
units.literal: The capital was shaken with terror; residents all left the city to hide, and the gatekeepers forbade it.

units.zh: 重美曰：「國家多難，不能與民為主，而欲禁其避禍，可乎？」
units.en: Chongmei said, “The realm is in grave trouble; we cannot protect the people, yet would forbid them to escape disaster—how can that be right?”
units.literal: Chongmei said: “The state is in great difficulty; we cannot act as masters for the people, yet would forbid them to flee harm—can that be right?”

units.zh: 因縱民出。
units.en: He therefore allowed the people to go out.
units.literal: He therefore let the people leave.

units.zh: 及晉兵將至，劉皇后積薪于地，將焚其宮室，重美曰：「新天子至，必不露坐，但佗日重勞民力，取怨身後耳！」
units.en: As the Jin army neared, Empress Liu heaped firewood to burn the palace. Chongmei said, “When the new emperor arrives he will not sit in the open air; this would only waste the people’s labor later and bring hatred after our deaths!”
units.literal: When the Jin army was about to arrive, Empress Liu piled firewood on the ground and was about to burn the palace halls. Chongmei said: “When the new Son of Heaven comes, he will surely not sit in the open; this would only later overburden the people’s strength and win resentment after death!”

units.zh: 后以為然。
units.en: The empress agreed.
units.literal: The empress thought him right.

units.zh: 廢帝自焚，后及重美與俱死。
units.en: The deposed emperor set himself afire; the empress and Chongmei perished with him.
units.literal: The Deposed Emperor burned himself; the empress and Chongmei died with him.

units.zh: 嗚呼！
units.en: Alas!
units.literal: Ah!

units.zh: 家人之道，不可不正也。
units.en: The norms that govern household and kin must be upheld.
units.literal: The way of the "Family" cannot fail to be set right.

units.zh: 夫禮者，所以別嫌而明微也。
units.en: Ritual exists precisely to dispel doubt and bring fine distinctions to light.
units.literal: Now ritual is that whereby one separates what is suspect and makes clear what is subtle.

units.zh: 甚矣，五代之際，君君臣臣父父子子之道乖，而宗廟、朝廷，人鬼皆失其序，斯可謂亂世者歟！
units.en: How far things had fallen! In the Five Dynasties the reciprocal duties of ruler and ruled, father and child, collapsed together; temple and palace alike were scenes where neither men nor shades kept their station—truly an era of disorder!
units.literal: Extreme! At the time of the Five Dynasties, the way of lord and lord, minister and minister, father and father, son and son went awry; at the ancestral temple and at court, both the living and the dead lost their proper order—this may indeed be called an age of chaos!

units.zh: 自古未之有也。
units.en: Nothing like it appears in the earlier record.
units.literal: From antiquity onward there has never been such a thing.

units.zh: 唐一號而三姓，周一號而二姓。
units.en: The house called Tang ruled under a single dynastic name yet passed through three clans; the house called Zhou did the same with two.
units.literal: Tang bore one reign title but three surnames; Zhou bore one reign title but two surnames.

units.zh: 唐太祖、莊宗為一家，明宗、湣帝為一家，廢帝為一家；
units.en: Later Tang thus falls into three bloodlines: Taizu and Zhuangzong; Mingzong and the short-reigned Min emperor; and the deposed emperor alone.
units.literal: Tang Taizu and Zhuangzong were one family; Mingzong and the Min Emperor were one family; the Deposed Emperor was one family;

units.zh: 周太祖為一家，世宗為一家。
units.en: Later Zhou likewise splits in two: the line of Taizu and that of Shizong.
units.literal: Zhou Taizu was one family, Shizong was one family.

units.zh: 別其家而同其號者，何哉？
units.en: Why, then, does the chronicle cleave the clans yet leave the dynastic label unchanged?
units.literal: They distinguish their families yet share the same dynastic name—why is that?

units.zh: 唐從其號，見其盜而有也；
units.en: For Later Tang the shared name exposes naked usurpation: each claimant seized the throne from the last.
units.literal: For Tang, following its name shows that they stole it yet came to possess it;

units.zh: 周從其號，與之也。
units.en: For Later Zhou the single title marks legitimate succession: the mandate was handed down within the alliance that founded the state.
units.literal: for Zhou, following its name means it was given to them.

units.zh: 而別其家者，昭穆親疏之不可亂也。
units.en: The separate "families" preserve the temple order of fathers and sons, near kin and far—lines that must not be blurred.
units.literal: But distinguishing their families is because senior and junior generations, close and distant kin, cannot be confused.

units.zh: 號可同，家不可以不別，所以別嫌而明微也。
units.en: Dynastic names may repeat; agnatic lines may not. That, again, is the work of ritual: clearing doubt and marking fine shades.
units.literal: The name may be the same; families cannot fail to be distinguished—this is to separate suspicion and clarify the subtle.

units.zh: 梁博王友文之不別，何哉？
units.en: Why, then, does the Later Liang record leave Bo Prince You Wen outside the neat partition of "families" that I have just defended?
units.literal: The Prince of Bo of Liang, You Wen—why was no family distinction drawn for him?

units.zh: 著禍本也，梁太祖之禍，自友文始，存之所以戒也。
units.en: Because the historian means to expose the taproot: the founder of Later Liang brought ruin on himself starting with You Wen, and the deliberate ambiguity in the record is itself the lesson for posterity.
units.literal: It is to write down the root of calamity: the calamity of Liang Taizu began with You Wen; keeping this unresolved exists in order to warn.

units.zh: 晉王遣都將李嗣昭、李存審、王建及率師來援同州，戰於城下。
units.en: The Prince of Jin sent Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji to relieve Tongzhou and battle was joined under the walls.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin sent commanders Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji with troops to relieve Tongzhou; they fought below the walls.

units.zh: 夏四月己巳，晉王即唐帝位於魏州，改天祐二十年為同光元年。
units.en: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin took the Tang throne at Weizhou, renaming Tianyou 20 Tongguang 1.
units.literal: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin assumed the Tang throne at Weizhou, changing Tianyou 20 to Tongguang 1.

units.zh: 時晉王方攻鎮州，故思遠乘虛以襲之，陷成安，而思遠遂急攻德勝北城，晉將李存審極力拒守。
units.en: While the Prince of Jin besieged Zhenzhou, Siyuan took Cheng'an and stormed Desheng’s north wall; Li Cunshen held firm.
units.literal: At the time the Prince of Jin was attacking Zhenzhou; hence Siyuan seized the opening to strike, took Cheng'an, and then urgently attacked Desheng’s northern city; Jin commander Li Cunshen resisted with utmost strength.

units.zh: 二月，晉王以兵至，思遠收軍而退，復保楊村。
units.en: In the second month the Prince of Jin came up; Siyuan withdrew to Yang village.
units.literal: In the second month the Prince of Jin arrived with troops; Siyuan gathered the army and withdrew, again holding Yang village.

units.zh: 唐帝棄德勝之北城，並軍保楊劉。
units.en: The Tang emperor abandoned Desheng’s north wall and concentrated at Yangliu.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor abandoned Desheng’s northern city and combined the army to hold Yangliu.

units.zh: 六月乙亥，唐帝引軍援楊劉，潛軍至博州，築壘於河東岸。
units.en: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang emperor relieved Yangliu while secretly fortifying east of Bozhou.
units.literal: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang Emperor led troops to relieve Yangliu, secretly moving the army to Bozhou and building ramparts on the river’s east bank.

units.zh: 秋七月丁未，唐帝引軍沿河而南。
units.en: On dingwei in the seventh month the Tang emperor led his army south along the river.
units.literal: On dingwei in the seventh month of autumn the Tang Emperor led troops south along the river.

units.zh: 庚寅，唐帝軍於胡城，先鋒將康延孝率百騎奔於唐，盡泄其軍機。
units.en: On gengyin at Hucheng vanguard Kang Yanxiao defected with a hundred riders and betrayed Liang dispositions.
units.literal: On gengyin the Tang Emperor’s army was at Hucheng; vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao led a hundred horsemen to defect to Tang and fully revealed our military plans.

units.zh: 甲戌，唐帝引師襲中都，王彥章兵潰，於是彥章與監軍張漢傑及趙廷隱、劉嗣彬、李知節、唐文通、王山興等皆為唐人所獲。
units.en: On jiaxu the Tang emperor stormed Zhongdu; Yanzhang’s army broke; he, Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, and others were taken.
units.literal: On jiaxu the Tang Emperor led troops to strike Zhongdu; Wang Yanzhang’s army collapsed; thereupon Yanzhang, army supervisor Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, Liu Sibin, Li Zhijie, Tang Wentong, Wang Shanxing, and others were all captured by Tang men.

units.zh: 帝置傳國寶於臥內，俄失其所在，已為左右所竊迎唐帝矣。
units.en: He laid the seal in his chamber; it vanished—courtiers had stolen it to greet the Tang emperor.
units.literal: The Emperor placed the dynastic seal in the sleeping chamber; soon it lost its place—it had already been stolen by attendants to welcome the Tang Emperor.

units.zh: 唐帝入宮，妃郭氏號泣迎拜。
units.en: The Tang emperor entered the palace; Consort Guo wept and bowed in welcome.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor entered the palace; consort Guo wailed and came forward to bow.

units.zh: 唐帝初入東京，聞帝殂，憮然歎曰：「敵惠敵怨，不在後嗣。
units.en: Entering the Eastern Capital, the Tang emperor learned of the Last Emperor’s death and sighed: "Grudges need not pass to sons.
units.literal: When the Tang Emperor first entered the Eastern Capital and heard the Emperor had died, he sighed in dejection: "Enemy kindness and enemy hatred do not lie in later generations.

units.zh: 九月庚寅，以供奉官郎公遠充契丹歡好使。
units.en: On gengyin in the ninth month Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was sent as envoy of goodwill to the Khitan.
units.literal: On gengyin in the ninth month, Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was made Khitan Goodwill envoy.

units.zh: 龍德二年春正月，戴思遠率師襲魏州。
units.en: In the first month of Longde 2 Dai Siyuan raided Weizhou.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of Longde 2, Dai Siyuan led troops to raid Weizhou.

units.zh: 尋詔河南尹張全義收葬之，其首藏於太社。
units.en: He ordered Zhang Quanyi to bury the body; the head was kept at the Grand Altar.
units.literal: Soon an edict ordered Henan Intendant Zhang Quanyi to collect and bury him; his head was stored at the Grand Altar.

units.zh: 先是，繼韜父嗣昭為潞州節度使，戰歿於鎮州城下，晉王欲以嗣昭長子繼儔襲父位。
units.en: His father Li Sizhao had held Luzhou and died at Zhenzhou; the Prince of Jin meant to give the post to eldest son Jichou.
units.literal: Earlier, Jiyao’s father Sizhao was Luzhou military commissioner and fell in battle below Zhenzhou city; the Prince of Jin wished to let Sizhao’s eldest son Jichou succeed his father’s post.

units.zh: 朕與梁主十年對壘，恨不生見其面。」
units.en: We fought ten years; I regret never meeting him alive."
units.literal: I and the Liang ruler faced each other in battle ten years, regretting I did not see his face in life."

units.zh: 以天雄軍節度使石敬瑭為御營使。
units.en: Shi Jingtang of Tianxiong became imperial camp commissioner.
units.literal: Tianxiong army military commissioner Shi Jingtang was made imperial camp commissioner.

units.zh: 壬戌，幽州節度使趙德鈞兼北面行營招討使，鎮州節度使範延光加檢校太傅。
units.en: On renxu Zhao Dejun of Youzhou became northern campaign commissioner and Fan Yanguang of Zhen inspector grand mentor.
units.literal: On renxu, Youzhou military commissioner Zhao Dejun was given added northern campaign headquarters commissioner; Zhen prefecture military commissioner Fan Yanguang was given Inspector Grand Mentor by inspection.

units.zh: 初，樞自歙州罷郡歸朝，路經大梁，時硃全忠兵威已振，樞以兄事之，全忠由是重之。
units.en: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.
units.literal: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.

units.zh: 制出，硃全忠保薦之，言樞有經世才，不可棄之嶺表，尋復拜門下侍郎，監修國史，累兼吏部尚書，判度支。
units.en: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed vice minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as minister of personnel, administering the treasury.
units.literal: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as Minister of Personnel, administering the treasury.

units.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。
units.en: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.
units.literal: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 時崔胤專政，亦倚全忠，二人因是相結，改樞吏部侍郎。
units.en: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 崔胤誅，以全忠素厚，相位如故。
units.en: After Cui Yin's execution, Shu's ties to Quanzhong kept him in the chancellorship unchanged.
units.literal: When Cui Yin was executed, because of his longstanding closeness to Quanzhong Shu's chancellorship remained unchanged.

units.zh: 延皓即劉後之弟也。
units.en: Yanhao was the younger brother of Empress Liu.
units.literal: Yanhao was the younger brother of Empress Liu.

units.zh: 時執政以延皓失守，請舉舊章，末帝以劉後內政之故，止從罷免而已，由是清泰之政弊矣。
units.en: At the time the chief ministers, because Yanhao had lost his command, asked to apply the old regulations; the Last Emperor, because of Empress Liu's influence in the inner court, only went so far as dismissal—thereby the government of Qingtai was harmed.
units.literal: At the time the chief ministers, because Yanhao had lost his command, asked to apply the old regulations; the Last Emperor, because of Empress Liu's influence in the inner court, only went so far as dismissal—thereby the government of Qingtai was harmed.

units.zh: 以樞密副使劉延朗為左領軍上將軍，充宣徽北院使兼樞密副使。
units.en: Liu Yanlang, Bureau of Military Affairs vice commissioner, was made General of the Left Army and Northern Bureau commissioner with his vice commissionership unchanged.
units.literal: Liu Yanlang, Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made General of the Left Army and assigned as Commissioner of the Northern Bureau and concurrent Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

units.zh: 以皇子河中留後從珂為河中節度使，百僚表賀。
units.en: Li Congke, Hezhong acting commissioner, became Hezhong commissioner; the court congratulated him.
units.literal: The Prince's Hedong acting military commissioner Congke was made Hedong military commissioner; the hundred officials memorialized congratulations.

units.zh: 以皇子河南尹、判六軍諸衛事從厚為北京留守；
units.en: Prince Conghou of Henan became Beijing regent;
units.literal: the prince, Henan intendant judging the Six Armies and all guards Conghou, was made Beijing regent;

units.zh: 是月，周主威殂，養子晉王柴榮嗣立。
units.en: That month Zhou's ruler Guo Wei died, and his adopted son, Prince of Jin Chai Rong, succeeded him.
units.literal: That month Zhou ruler Wei died; his adopted son, Prince of Jin Chai Rong, succeeded to the throne.

units.zh: 是月，周主榮殂，子宗訓立。
units.en: That month Zhou's ruler Rong died and his son Zongxun succeeded to the throne.
units.literal: That month, Zhou's ruler Rong died and his son Zongxun succeeded to the throne.

units.zh: 時李嗣源總帳下親軍攻東北隅；
units.en: Li Siyuan led the household guard against the northeast corner;
units.literal: Li Siyuan commanded the personal troops below the tent attacking the northeast corner;

units.zh: 李嗣源壞夾城東北隅，率先掩擊，梁軍大恐，南向而奔，投戈委甲，噎塞行路，斬萬餘級，獲其將副招討使符道昭洎大將三百人，芻粟百萬。
units.en: Li Siyuan breached Jiacity's northeast and charged in; Liang panicked and fled south, shedding arms until the road jammed; over ten thousand were killed; Fu Daozhao and three hundred officers were taken, with a million bundles of fodder.
units.literal: Li Siyuan broke the northeast corner of Jiacity and led the assault; the Liang army was greatly terrified and fled south, casting weapons and armor; the road was choked; more than ten thousand were beheaded; deputy pacification commissioner Fu Daozhao and three hundred great generals were captured, and a million measures of fodder.

units.zh: 五月辛未朔，晨霧晦暝，帝率親軍伏三垂崗下。
units.en: At the xinwei new moon in the fifth month, thick morning fog hid Cunxu's personal troops below Sanchui Ridge.
units.literal: On the first day xinwei of the fifth month, morning fog dark and dim, the Emperor led his personal army in ambush below Sanchui Ridge.

units.zh: 延皓禦軍失政，為屯將張令昭所逐，出奔相州，尋詔停所任。
units.en: Yanhao governed the army badly; the garrison officer Zhang Lingzhao expelled him, he fled to Xiangzhou, and soon an edict stripped him of office.
units.literal: Yanhao governed the army badly; the garrison officer Zhang Lingzhao expelled him, he fled to Xiangzhou, and soon an edict stripped him of office.

units.zh: 及出鎮大名，而所執一變，掠人財賄，納人園宅，聚歌僮為長夜之飲，而三軍所給不時，內外怨之，因為令昭所逐。
units.en: But when he went out to command at Daming his conduct changed entirely: he seized people's wealth as bribes, took their gardens and residences, gathered singing boys for all-night drinking, and paid the three armies' supplies irregularly; inside and outside complained of him, and thereby he was expelled by Lingzhao.
units.literal: But when he went out to command at Daming his conduct changed entirely: he seized people's wealth as bribes, took their gardens and residences, gathered singing boys for all-night drinking, and paid the three armies' supplies irregularly; inside and outside complained of him, and thereby he was expelled by Lingzhao.

units.zh: 以蕃漢兵馬都孔目官郭威為權樞密使、檢校司徒；
units.en: Guo Wei was made acting Commissioner of Military Affairs and Acting Minister of Works;
units.literal: Guo Wei, chief clerk of tribal and Han forces, was made acting Commissioner of Military Affairs and Acting Minister of Works;

units.zh: 庚辰，皇孫太子舍人重美授司勳員外郎，重真已下六人並授同正將軍及檢校官。
units.en: On gengchen imperial grandson Chongmei, crown prince aide, became vice director of merit; Chongzhen and six below received honorary regular general and acting commissioner posts.
units.literal: On gengchen, the imperial grandson and crown prince aide Chongmei was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Merit; Chongzhen and six others below were all made honorary regular generals and acting commissioners.

units.zh: 辛卯，以宣徽南院使劉延皓為刑部尚書，充樞密使；
units.en: On xinmao Liu Yanhao, Southern Bureau commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was made Minister of Justice and Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner;
units.literal: On xinmao, Liu Yanhao, Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made Minister of Justice and assigned as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs;

units.zh: 《通鑒》：乙卯，博王友文來朝，請帝還東都。
units.en: 《Comprehensive Mirror》: On yimao the Prince of Bo, Youwen, attended court and urged the Emperor to return east.
units.literal: 《Comprehensive Mirror》: On yimao Prince of Bo Youwen came to court and asked the Emperor to return to the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 己巳，至東都，博王友文以新創食殿上言，並進準備內宴錢三千貫、銀器一千五百兩。
units.en: On jisi he arrived at the Eastern Capital; Prince of Bo Youwen reported on the new Dining Hall and presented three thousand strings of cash and fifteen hundred taels of silver for an inner banquet.
units.literal: On jisi he reached the Eastern Capital; Prince of Bo Youwen memorialized on the newly built Dining Hall and also presented three thousand strings of cash and fifteen hundred taels of silverware prepared for an inner banquet.

units.zh: 制加建昌宮使、金紫光祿大夫、檢校司徒、開封尹、博王友文為特進、檢校太保，兼開封尹，依前建昌宮使，充東都留守。
units.en: By order Youwen, Prince of Bo, Jianchang palace commissioner, golden-seal grand master of splendid happiness, honorary grand mentor, and Kaifeng intendant, was raised to special court attendance and honorary grand guardian, kept Kaifeng intendant, and remained Jianchang commissioner and Eastern Capital custodian.
units.literal: An order advanced Jianchang Palace Commissioner, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Honorary Grand Mentor, Kaifeng Intendant, and Prince of Bo Youwen to Special Court Attendance and Honorary Grand Guardian, also Kaifeng Intendant, continuing as Jianchang Palace Commissioner and Eastern Capital Custodian.

units.zh: 次假子友文，帝特愛之，常留守東都，兼建昌宮使。
units.en: Next came the adopted son Youwen, the Emperor's favorite, who often stayed at the Eastern Capital as Jianchang palace commissioner.
units.literal: Next was the adopted son Youwen, whom the Emperor especially loved; he often remained at the Eastern Capital as Jianchang Palace Commissioner.

units.zh: 己卯，矯詔稱：「博王友文謀逆，遣兵突入殿中，賴郢王友珮忠孝，將兵誅之，保全朕躬。
units.en: On jimao a forged edict read: "Prince of Bo Youwen plotted revolt and burst into the hall with troops; Prince of Ying Yougui, loyal and filial, led forces to execute them and saved Us.
units.literal: On jimao a forged edict stated: "Prince of Bo Youwen plotted rebellion and sent troops bursting into the hall; thanks to Prince of Ying Yougui’s loyalty and filial piety, who led troops to execute them and preserved Our person.

units.zh: 遣供奉官丁昭溥馳詣東都，命均王友貞殺友文。
units.en: He sent palace attendant Ding Zhaopu in haste to the Eastern Capital to order Prince of Jun Youzhen to kill Youwen.
units.literal: He dispatched Palace Attendant Ding Zhaopu posthaste to the Eastern Capital ordering Prince of Jun Youzhen to kill Youwen.

units.zh: 辛巳，丁昭溥還，聞友文已死，乃發喪，宣遺制，友珪即皇帝位。
units.en: On xinsi Ding Zhaopu returned; learning Youwen was dead, they announced mourning, proclaimed the testament, and Yougui seized the throne.
units.literal: On xinsi Ding Zhaopu returned; hearing Youwen was already dead, they then announced the mourning, proclaimed the testamentary order, and Yougui at once took the throne.

units.zh: 帝雖未以友文為太子，意常屬之。
units.en: Youwen was not named crown prince, yet the Emperor's heart was often set on him.
units.literal: Although the Emperor had not made Youwen crown prince, his intent often rested on him.

units.zh: 重吉，末帝長子，為控鶴都指揮使。
units.en: Chongji, the Last Emperor's eldest son, was director of the Crane-Control Directorate.
units.literal: Chongji, the Last Emperor's eldest son, served as director of the Crane-Control Directorate.

units.zh: 匡祚榜捶重吉，責其家財。）〉
units.en: Kuangzuo beat Chongji with cudgels and extorted his family's wealth.)〉
units.literal: Kuangzuo beat Chongji with cudgels and extorted his family's wealth.)〉

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：詔遣殿直楚匡祚執亳州李重吉，幽於宋州。
units.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror records that an edict dispatched Palace Guard Chu Kuangzuo to arrest Li Chongji of Bozhou and imprison him at Songzhou.
units.literal: (The Comprehensive Mirror states: An edict dispatched Palace Guard Chu Kuangzuo to arrest Li Chongji of Bozhou and imprison him at Songzhou.

units.zh: 又云：遣楚匡祚殺李重吉於宋州。
units.en: It also records that Chu Kuangzuo was sent to kill Li Chongji at Songzhou.
units.literal: It also states: Chu Kuangzuo was sent to kill Li Chongji at Songzhou.

units.zh: 清泰元年，詔贈太尉，仍令宋州選隙地置廟。
units.en: In Qingtai 1 an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Marshal and ordered Songzhou to select vacant land for a temple.
units.literal: In the first year of Qingtai, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Marshal and ordered Songzhou to select vacant land on which to establish a temple.

units.zh: 閔帝嗣位，出為亳州團練使。
units.en: When Emperor Min succeeded, he was posted out as training commissioner of Bozhou.
units.literal: When Emperor Min succeeded to the throne, he was posted out as training commissioner of Bozhou.

units.zh: 末帝兵起，為閔帝所害。
units.en: When the Last Emperor raised his army, Emperor Min had him killed.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor raised his army, he was killed by Emperor Min.
